description:
Our international correspondent John Sparks breaks down the debate over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands - a controversy that came to the surface at the end of Argentina and England's World Cup semi-final.

comments.text:
The Spanish name for the Falkland Islands, Malvinas, ultimately comes from the French Malouines, named after Saint-Malo in Brittany. Saint Malo himself was born in Wales, which is part of Britain, making it rather ironic that Argentina’s preferred name ultimately commemorates someone from Britain.

Even better, “Malvinas” sounds like mal viñas (“bad vines”), which makes the phrase “sour grapes” feel especially appropriate given Argentina’s continuing claim to the islands.
